singular VERSION (commit unknown)

Usage: singular registry address [--config FILE] [--registry ADDRESS]
       [--state-token POLICY.NAME] [--network-magic N] [--trace LEVEL]
       [--trace-to SINK] [--trace-format FORMAT]

Show or make a registry's address

Prints one receipt about a registry: its address, its state token, its
fingerprint and its network magic. Given the address (--registry) it shows
what the address holds; given a state token and a network magic it makes the
address, for a registry created before addresses were printed. It reads no
chain and needs no provider.

The prefix of an address names the network: singular for mainnet,
singular_preprod for preprod, singular_preview for preview and singular_devnet
for the generated development network. A network magic that has no prefix is
refused.

Available settings:
  Show this help text
  switch: -h|--help

  A JSON file giving the settings the command line and the environment leave
  out.
  option: --config FILE
  env: SINGULAR_CONFIG FILE
  default: singular.json in the working directory, if there is one

  The registry to act on: its address, as create prints it. The address holds
  the state token and the network, so a command given it needs neither.
  option: --registry ADDRESS
  env: SINGULAR_REGISTRY ADDRESS
  config:
    registry: # or null
      <string>

  The registry to act on: its state token, policy and name in hex, as create
  prints it.
  option: --state-token POLICY.NAME
  env: SINGULAR_STATE_TOKEN POLICY.NAME
  config:
    state-token: # or null
      <string>

  The network: 1 for preprod, 42 for the generated development network.
  option: --network-magic N
  env: SINGULAR_NETWORK_MAGIC N
  config:
    network-magic: # or null
      <string>

  How much to narrate: off, what (protocol steps) or how (also their
  mechanics).
  option: --trace LEVEL
  env: SINGULAR_TRACE LEVEL
  config:
    trace: # or null
      <string>
  default: what on a terminal, otherwise off

  Where the narration goes: stderr or file:PATH; repeat for several.
  option: --trace-to SINK
  env: SINGULAR_TRACE_TO SINK
  config:
    trace-to: # or null
      <string>
  default: stderr

  The format of the narration: text for a person, json for a program.
  option: --trace-format FORMAT
  env: SINGULAR_TRACE_FORMAT FORMAT
  config:
    trace-format: # or null
      <string>
  default: text on standard error, json in a file

Where settings come from:
  A setting with an env and a config line above is given in any of three ways,
  and the first that is present wins: the flag, then the variable, then the
  key in the config file, then the default.

  The file is one JSON object whose keys are the setting names without their
  dashes, text or numbers, for example

    {"koios-url": "https://preprod.koios.rest/api/v1", "network-magic": 1}

  It is singular.json in the working directory, or the file named by --config
  or SINGULAR_CONFIG. A path in it means what it means on the command line,
  from where the command runs. A passphrase is never read from the file; the
  environment gives one only on a development network, as SINGULAR_PASSPHRASE.

Environment:
  SINGULAR_LOG  A file the protocol phases are appended to, one line each.

Example:
  singular registry address \
      --state-token <policy>.<name> --network-magic 1

  With those settings in singular.json instead:
  singular registry address

Output and exit status:
  Prints the receipt alone and writes no file.
  Exit status 0 on success, 2 for a command line it refused.
